title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.

providers.name: DocuSign eSignature
providers.scope_notes: Organization/domain-management entitlements apply. CLM IP restrictions and Monitor alerts do not prove eSignature API enforcement.

controls.name: Connected Apps > Authorize Application (admin consent)
controls.what: Org admin grants consent for an org-owned integration key on behalf of all claimed-domain users, limited to the permissions (OAuth scopes) entered, e.g. signature impersonation.
controls.setting: Docusign Admin > Organization > Connected Apps > Authorize Application
controls.plan: Docusign Admin with Access Management (org + claimed domain)
controls.quote: These permissions define the OAuth scopes the application can access. An example is "signature".

controls.name: Connected Apps > Edit an Authorized Application
controls.what: Changes the permissions (scopes) granted to an admin-authorized app.
controls.setting: Docusign Admin > Organization > Connected Apps > Actions > Edit
controls.plan: Docusign Admin with Access Management (org + claimed domain)
controls.quote: You can edit the Permissions settings for an authorized application.

controls.name: Connected Apps > Revoke Authorization
controls.what: Removes an admin-authorized app and revokes its consent for all domain users; refresh tokens die, live access tokens run to expiry.
controls.setting: Docusign Admin > Organization > Connected Apps > Actions > Revoke
controls.plan: Docusign Admin with Access Management (org + claimed domain)
controls.quote: The application is removed from your organization and access is revoked for all domain users.

controls.name: Require all users to log in with SSO only
controls.what: Forces claimed-domain users to authenticate through the IdP, so authorization-code logins go through SSO.
controls.setting: Docusign Admin > Organization > Domains > Actions > Manage Settings > Login Settings > Single Sign-On
controls.quote: Require all users to log in with SSO only : If enabled, this setting removes the Use Company Login button and automatically redirects your users to your organization’s identity provider.

controls.name: Restrict Domain IPs (Allowed IP Ranges)
controls.what: Restricts login and authentication traffic for claimed-domain users to up to 30 IPv4 ranges.
controls.setting: Docusign Admin > Organization > Domains > Actions > Manage Settings > Access Settings > Add IP Range; toggle Allowed IP Ranges
controls.plan: Docusign Admin org with claimed domain (section notes Access Management with SSO add-on)
controls.quote: Organization administrators can set a domain level policy for claimed domain users and restrict login and authentication traffic by IP addresses. This IP range restriction applies to both password login and SSO login.

controls.name: Permission profile: Allow view and manage envelope rights through API
controls.what: When unchecked, users with the profile cannot view/manage all account envelopes via the API (account-wide API access).
controls.quote: Allow view and manage envelope rights through API : When selected, the user can: View, manage, and request the status of all envelopes for the account through the Docusign API.

controls.name: Permission profile setting allowApiAccessToAccount
controls.what: When false, users with the profile cannot access the account through the eSignature API.
controls.setting: eSignature REST API: AccountPermissionProfiles settings.allowApiAccessToAccount (UI label not verified)
controls.quote: allowApiAccessToAccount: When true, users can access the account by using the eSignature API.

controls.name: Apps and Keys (integration key secrets, RSA keypairs, redirect URIs)
controls.what: Account admins manage the integration keys; removing secrets or RSA keypairs stops new auth-code or JWT token requests for that key.
controls.setting: eSignature Admin > Integrations > Apps and Keys
controls.quote: After a key has been moved to the Production environment, the account it is linked to is used to manage secret keys, RSA keypairs, and redirect URIs.

no_control.what: Admin consent via the Connected Apps UI only covers org-owned integration keys; external apps need a special consent flow.
no_control.quote: Note: For external integrations, consent cannot be granted from the UI.

controls_unknown: Whether Restrict Domain IPs or SSO-only login apply to JWT grant token requests (no user login occurs) or to API calls with an existing token.
Whether admins can stop users from granting individual consent to arbitrary integration keys (no allowlist/block setting found).

authentication.summary: OAuth authorization code + PKCE or JWT grant. JWT grant impersonates a consenting user with an app private key.

federation.details: SAML login and app-signed JWT impersonation do not establish generic external IdP/workload-token federation.

ip_restriction.boundary: Claimed-domain IP restrictions are documented for password/SSO authentication. Per-request eSignature bearer-token IP enforcement was not verified.

renewal.summary: Refresh token (typically about 30 days from first login, not reset on use). With the extended scope, each refresh issues a token with a full new lifetime, so access can continue while the token is used before expiry. Password change or consent revocation can invalidate it.

administration.summary: OAuth scopes/consent, user permission profiles and application access. Domain/IP settings and session controls are separate.
administration.conditions: Organization/domain-management entitlements apply. CLM IP restrictions and Monitor alerts do not prove eSignature API enforcement.

sso.details: The user signs in on the Docusign sign-in screen to grant the code, and SSO-only domains redirect that sign-in to the IdP; refresh tokens then renew without a new login for about 30 days.

inventory.details: Each user sees their own consented apps under Manage Profile > Connected Apps; admin-granted consents are managed in Docusign Admin. No org-wide list of user-granted consents documented.

sso.ui: Admin > Domains > (domain) ACTIONS > Manage Settings > Settings > Login Settings > SSO Login Requirement: Require all users to log in with SSO only; per-user exceptions under Users > View User > Security

expiry.api: Fixed; read expires_in in the POST https://account.docusign.com/oauth/token response

usage.ui: Admin > Organization > Monitor > User Investigations; filter by User and Event (paid Monitor)

reads.ui: Admin > Organization > Monitor > User Investigations; Event = Document downloaded
reads.api: GET https://api.docusign.com/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/stream; filter events named Document downloaded

token_format.notes: Opaque bearer access token (8 h default for Authorization Code Grant) plus refresh token. Integration key (client id) is a GUID. Not in GitHub's secret scanning partner list.

log_sources.name: Docusign Monitor (Monitor API stream)
log_sources.notes: Org-level security events incl. API-driven actions; carries integratorKey per event. Licensing/edition and retention not established. Caller must use JWT impersonating an org admin.

credential_id_fields.notes: Integration key (OAuth client id) of the app that made the call
Docusign user the token acts as
Event source; value set not established

anomaly_cues: First event for an integratorKey not in the approved app inventory
Known integratorKey used from a new IP/country or new userAgent family
Same user's token used by an integratorKey they never consented to (check Connected Apps)
Bulk envelope download/export actions driven by an integration key outside business hours
API activity continuing after consent revoked (expected only until token expiry, ~8 h)

containment.steps: User: Manage Profile > Connected Apps > Revoke. Org-granted consent: revoke in Docusign Admin. If client secret leaked: revoke secrets on the integration key (Apps and Keys) and, if needed, ask Docusign to disable the key.
containment.notes: Revoking consent invalidates refresh tokens and blocks new tokens, but live access tokens keep working until they expire (8 h default for auth code).
